cases.question: xs-rs MVP: a Linux client and server that copy trees to and from the C++ xs, at least as fast
cases.summary: Added the xs-rs binary crate with a Linux client and server that speak the C++ xs version 4 stream in both directions. A C++ client can push to and pull from xs-rs, and xs-rs can push to and pull from a C++ xs server; trees compare equal including modes, nanosecond mtimes, symlinks, empty entries and non-UTF-8 names, with compressed and no-op transfers verified.

cases.question: zstd: compressed directory listings and data blocks (PF_ZSTD)
cases.summary: Ported the PF_ZSTD compression policy into xs-rs: exact C++ suffix-list parsing, F_COMPRESS_CONFIG negotiation and refusal, compression sampling, adaptive levels, and per-suffix isolation of raw DATA blocks. Rust clients and servers now exchange ZSTD directory listings and data blocks with the C++ xs and refuse hostile or unnegotiated compression frames.

cases.question: user and group names (PF_IDMAP, PF_CHOWN)
cases.summary: Implemented PF_IDMAP name records and PF_CHOWN ownership configuration in xs-rs, matching remote.cpp and ownership.cpp. The C++ client can now push/pull names and --chown overrides to/from xs-rs, and hostile or unnegotiated ownership frames are refused with the reference exit codes.

cases.question: keepalives, bandwidth limits and timeouts (PF_IO_CONTROL)
cases.summary: Implemented PF_IO_CONTROL in xs-rs: exact --bwlimit/--timeout parsing, the token-bucket rate limiter, F_IO_CONFIG negotiation in the C++ order, negotiated keep-alives, and idle-timeout exit code 30. C++ clients and servers interoperate in both directions, and hostile or older peers are refused for invalid or unnegotiated keep-alives and malformed I/O configuration.

cases.question: itemized output and progress (PF_OUTPUT, PF_DIR_OUTPUT, PF_PROGRESS_ACK)
cases.summary: Added the itemized-output and progress-acknowledgment protocol to xs-rs and xs-wire. C++ clients now get itemized events from xs-rs receivers, xs-rs clients render C++ receiver events, DIR frames carry the negotiated output metadata, and progress acknowledgments are bounded and feature-gated. All three gate commands pass with XS_BIN set to the parent C++ xs.

cases.question: hard links (PF_HLINK)
cases.summary: Implemented PF_HLINK in xs-rs: DIR entries and DATA file attributes now carry the C++ hdev/ino/nlink/ctime/ctime_ns fields, -H negotiates the feature, and the receiver groups source inodes, sends each group's data once, links aliases after transfer, and itemizes them exactly as the C++ xs does. Cross-direction C++/Rust push, pull and local copies preserve hard-link topology, including symlink and FIFO aliases.

cases.question: xs-rs performance: beat xs-c++ on congress-sample update-10pct
cases.summary: xs-rs now packs small DATA records across directory NEEDs instead of flushing one tiny DATA frame per NEED, and automatic compression no longer spends zstd on kilobyte-sized listings. On a 2-CPU, 11 ms-RTT race of the congress-sample update-10pct shape it improved from 1.61 s to 1.43 s against the parent binary, with CPU down about 13%. Explicit -z still compresses every listing as before.

cases.question: xs-rs performance: beat xs-c++ on congress-sample update-10pct
cases.summary: The change makes the xs-rs sender behave like xs-c++ at two points on the update path: it flushes a partial DATA block when its worker goes idle, and automatic compression can no longer escalate to zstd level 6 after a transient writer stall. Local update-10pct races were already ahead of xs-c++ and stayed within noise, but the change targets the lab's slow block, where xs-rs sent 5.75 MB instead of 7.54 MB and burned more CPU, consistent with a level-6 feedback stall.
